source: Statistics Canada, General Social Survey on Families, public-use microdata files: Cycle 10 (1995), Cycle 20 (2006), Cycle 25 (2011) and Cycle 31 (2017); retrospective marriage histories of people 15-79 in the ten provinces. Contains information licensed under the Statistics Canada Open Licence.
target: Annual rate of first-marriage dissolution (separation, or divorce/annulment without a recorded separation) per marriage-year from the wedding; widowhood and the interview censor (Poisson rate, not a probability)
population: Canadian household population aged 15-79 at interview (1995, 2006, 2011 or 2017) who had married; their FIRST marriage, weddings 1950-2017, the respondent's own report (men and women)
weights: GSS person weights, rescaled to mean 1 within each cycle, times exposure

inputs.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = first year)
inputs.age_at_marriage: the respondent's age in years on the wedding day (one partner: the model is respondent-level)
inputs.wedding_year: calendar year of the wedding; outside the support is extrapolation, so hold it at the support edge and say so
inputs.respondent_sex: Female/Male: the partner whose characteristics are entered
inputs.cohabited_first: Yes/No: lived common-law with this spouse before marrying
inputs.prior_union: Yes/No: had lived common-law with someone else before this first marriage
inputs.premarital_birth: Yes/No: had a birth child before the wedding
inputs.intact_family_15: Yes/No: lived with both parents until age 15
inputs.first_language: English, French, Other, Multiple: first language learned in childhood (2017: mother tongue)
inputs.region: Atlantic, Quebec, Ontario, Prairies, British Columbia: region of residence AT INTERVIEW (may postdate the marriage)
inputs.survey_cycle: GSS cycle; set to '2017' (app_defaults) when scoring a new couple

not_used_in_models.partner_age_gap: spouse's age is missing far more often for dissolved than intact marriages (see missingness_by_outcome.csv) and not asked for ended marriages in 2006; sensitivity only
not_used_in_models.partner_previously_married: asked for ended first marriages only in 1995; 1995-only sensitivity
not_used_in_models.education: highest education is measured at interview and can postdate the marriage (as in the NSFG lens); descriptive and sensitivity only
not_used_in_models.religion_and_attendance: measured at interview; can change with a divorce; descriptive and sensitivity only
not_used_in_models.birth_cohort: equals wedding_year minus age_at_marriage exactly, so it adds nothing beyond those two inputs

abstain: previously married (only first marriages are modelled)
same-sex couples (too few first marriages in these files)
age at marriage outside the support
outside Canada: population is the ten provinces
note: Pooled from four cross-sections with a survey-cycle term. Each respondent reports one marriage, so a couple is scored through one partner at a time. Separations are counted as dissolution, as in the NSFG lens.

population_reference.method: Held-out (5-fold, by person) predicted probability that the first marriage dissolves within 5, 10 and 20 years of the wedding from the gradient_boosting model; survey-weighted quantiles; cells with fewer than 100 unweighted marriages are not published; Unknown levels are omitted. n = unweighted marriages.

ood.method: squared Mahalanobis distance on the model inputs; percentile against held-out people (5 person folds)

models_extended.label: Additive spline Poisson, current inputs with the detailed family of origin

heldout.evaluation: train_models.py person folds (5); paired person bootstrap (1000)

models_extended_note: Held-out comparison (2026-10-20, extended_predictors.py). Only the family-of-origin model is exported: religion is measured at the interview, after many dissolutions, so it is never a scoring input. Blocks whose held-out difference had a 95% CI above zero: religion at interview (+0.51 points, but it is reported after many dissolutions, so this is not a valid prospective gain: people who separate attend less afterwards); family of origin: no (-0.00 points).

inputs_extended.family_origin: who the respondent grew up with to 15: Both parents / Parents divorced or separated (before 15; 2017 only) / Parent died (before 15; 2017 only) / Never-married parents (never married to each other; 2006-2017) / Not intact, reason not known / Unknown (incl. 1995)
